reference.source: Bradley and Daroff Neurology in Clinical Practice
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in VPS13A, which encodes chorein, a large protein implicated in lipid transfer at membrane contact sites and red-cell membrane integrity
Typically presents in early adulthood with a hyperkinetic movement disorder combining generalised chorea with prominent orofacial and lingual dyskinesia
Feeding dystonia, in which tongue thrusting expels food, is a characteristic and near-specific clue
Self-mutilating tongue, lip and cheek biting is a well-recognised feature
Peripheral blood film may show acanthocytes, and serum creatine kinase is frequently raised, reflecting a subclinical myopathy
Seizures, peripheral neuropathy, cognitive decline and neuropsychiatric features (obsessive-compulsive symptoms, apathy) are commonly associated
Absent or markedly reduced chorein on Western blot of erythrocyte membranes supports the diagnosis, confirmed by VPS13A genetic testing
reference.pathophysiology: Chorea-acanthocytosis results from biallelic pathogenic variants in VPS13A on chromosome 9q21, which encodes chorein, a bridge-like protein thought to mediate bulk lipid transfer between organelle membranes and to maintain the red-cell cytoskeleton. Loss of functional chorein produces deformed, spiculated erythrocytes (acanthocytes) and progressive neurodegeneration that preferentially affects the striatum, especially the caudate nucleus and putamen. Striatal neuronal loss and gliosis disrupt basal-ganglia circuits, generating chorea and dystonia, while associated myopathic and neuropathic changes reflect the wider tissue requirement for chorein.
additionalDifferentials: Huntington disease and Huntington disease-like syndromes
Pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration and other NBIA disorders
additionalInvestigations: Peripheral blood film examined under wet-film conditions for acanthocytes
Serum creatine kinase, which is often elevated
Western blot for chorein on erythrocyte membranes
Brain MRI to demonstrate caudate atrophy and striatal signal change
Nerve conduction studies and electromyography for associated neuropathy and myopathy
redFlags: Progressive cognitive and behavioural decline suggesting advancing neurodegeneration
Recurrent seizures that may be difficult to control
Severe feeding dystonia risking malnutrition and aspiration
Sudden clinical deterioration raising concern for cardiac involvement or status epilepticus
reference.prognosis: Chorea-acanthocytosis is a progressive, life-limiting neurodegenerative disorder that typically advances over one to two decades, with increasing disability from movement, cognitive and psychiatric features. Management is supportive and symptomatic, and premature death often relates to seizures, aspiration or intercurrent complications.
pitfalls: A single normal blood film does not exclude the diagnosis, as acanthocytes may be intermittent and require specific incubated wet-film technique
Mislabelling the disorder as Huntington disease when family history is uninformative or recessive inheritance is not considered
Overlooking a raised creatine kinase and attributing it to unrelated muscle injury
Assuming normal chorein levels exclude related neuroacanthocytosis such as McLeod syndrome, which requires separate testing
references: Bradley and Daroff Neurology in Clinical Practice
Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology
management: No disease-modifying treatment exists, so care is supportive and directed at symptoms
Control chorea with dopamine-depleting agents such as tetrabenazine or with dopamine-receptor antagonists
Treat dystonia and feeding dystonia with botulinum toxin and protective measures, and provide a mouthguard to limit tongue, lip and cheek self-mutilation
Manage seizures with antiepileptic drugs and treat neuropsychiatric features such as obsessive-compulsive symptoms and apathy
Support nutrition and swallowing with speech and language therapy and gastrostomy feeding to prevent aspiration
Consider deep brain stimulation for severe, refractory movement symptoms in selected patients
Provide genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance and coordinate multidisciplinary neurological, psychiatric and rehabilitation care
